lines: Caravanserais, however, were not always safe. Travellers (7) faced the risk of robbery, and local rulers sometimes (8) subjected merchants to heavy taxes. Roads were built (9) so that traders could reach inns more easily, and the inns themselves were designed around a central courtyard, with a (10) meeting place where news and goods were (11) as a result exchanged. This made the caravanserai a place of (12) exchange — of goods, of money, and (13) as well as of stories, ideas and religions, thus (14) influencing the cultures on both sides of the trade route.
然而，商队旅馆并不总是安全。旅行者（7）面临被劫掠的风险，当地统治者有时还（8）向商人课以重税。人们修建道路（9）以便商贾更容易到达客栈；客栈本身围绕中央庭院设计，设有（10）聚会场所，消息和货物（11）因而在此得以交换。这使商队旅馆成为一个（12）交流之地——交换货物、金钱，（13）也交换故事、思想与宗教，从而（14）影响着商路两端的文明。

lines: [A] In 1870, little was known about the Yellowstone country in the Wyoming Territory. Rumours told of a place where rivers ran through deep canyons, hot springs steamed in the forests, and a mountain lake stretched to the horizon. Fur trappers' tales of such wonders had long been dismissed as exaggerations, and no official survey had ever been conducted there.
